newsitem.title: USA: Fremont to buy Xerox insurance unit.
newsitem.headline: Fremont to buy Xerox insurance unit.

text.p: Fremont General Corp. has a definitive agreement to buy Industrial Indemnity Holdings Inc. from a subsidiary of Xerox Corp. in a deal worth $444 million, the companies said Monday.

Fremont, one of the nation's largest underwriters of workers' compensation insurance, will pay Talegen Holdings Inc. $365 million in cash and pay off $79 million that Industrial Indemnity owes Talegen.
Industrial Indemnity, based in San Francisco, provides underwriting worker's compensation insurance and risk management services. It has about 850 employees in 19 offices.
Xerox said the purchase price is more than the book value of Industrial Indemnity and is consistent with the estimated value of the unit when Xerox discontinued its insurance operations in 1995.
Fremont, based in Santa Monica, Calif., said financing for the deal will come from internal funds and bank borrowings.
Fremont's stock rose $1.50 to $30.125, while Xerox edged up 25 cents to $63 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
